title: Customs System Failure Halts Cargo at Nuevo Laredo's World Trade Bridge for Two Hours
excerpt: Export operations at Nuevo Laredo's World Trade Bridge were paralyzed for about two hours after a failure in Mexico's National Customs Agency system, snarling cross-border trade and backing up traffic on Loop 20 in Laredo.
content:
Export operations at the World Trade International Bridge in Nuevo Laredo were paralyzed for about two hours on Wednesday afternoon, Nov. 25, after a failure in the system of Mexico's National Customs Agency, known as ANAM, according to Con Lupa.

Francisco Elizondo, a state counselor for the National Chamber of Freight Transportation, known as Canacar, said cargo gradually began crossing again as the system came back. The outage disrupted the flow of trade with the United States and caused congestion on both sides of the border.

ANAM activated a contingency program that allowed shipments to be processed using earlier formats, while traffic control units helped manage the area as service was restored. Customs agents and carriers reported that the failure was nationwide, not limited to Nuevo Laredo.

The Laredo Police Department warned of significant lines on Loop 20 westbound and urged drivers to avoid the road if they were not traveling in a commercial vehicle.

Carriers say interruptions like this one have happened in previous months, costing them waiting time, fuel and delivery delays. The bridge is one of the busiest crossings for bilateral trade, and traffic began flowing gradually again by late afternoon.

The authority has not detailed the exact cause of the failure or the total number of units affected, and carriers are hoping the system stabilizes fully to avoid new backups in the coming days.

Sources: Con Lupa, Nov. 27, 2026.
